title: Request shaping feedback loop and SLO tuning playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook defines an end-to-end pattern for shaping incoming inference requests, measuring the impact on SLOs and cost, and applying an automated feedback loop to tune shaping parameters. It consolidates API-level rules, runtime configuration, observability signals, and a human-operated escalation path. The goal is to keep 99th-percentile latency and error-rate SLOs within target while reducing GPU token cost under variable load.

Scope
- Applies to public-facing text generation and chat endpoints served by the inference runtime (hosted + dedicated).
- Excludes long-running batch jobs and offline embedding pipelines.
- Targets dynamic shaping (per-tenant and per-route) and autoscaling policies that depend on shaping signals.

Motivation
- Traffic bursts with pathological prompt lengths drive tail latency and knee-of-costs on some model variants.
- Coarse autoscaling alone is slow and increases cost; shaping reduces transient load and exposes high-latency requests for special handling.

SLOs and thresholds
- Latency SLOs (per-route): p50 < 60ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 650ms (for standard routes).
- Error SLO: successful response rate >= 99.5% over 5m windows.
- Cost signal: tokens-per-second per-GPU target (soft) based on model class.

Minimal telemetry set (required)
- request.latency_ms (histogram)
- request.status (ok|error|cancelled|throttled)
- request.payload_tokens (gauge)
- tenant.queue_depth (gauge)
- shaping.action (none|reject|defer|reduce_model|truncate_prefix)
- model.variant_in_use (tag)

Request shaping policy (runtime-level)
1) Admission: fast reject for requests that exceed hard limits (payload_tokens > 120k or seq_len > 512k). Returns 413 with structured error.
2) Adaptive per-tenant rate cap: token-rate cap computed from commit/plan and recent 1h utilization.
3) Degradation path: when queue_depth > Q_THRESH or p95 latency > LATENCY_THRESH, apply progressive actions:
   a. truncate optional context (policy: preserve final 512 tokens)
   b. switch to cheaper model variant (maintain structured response schema)
   c. return throttled response with Retry-After header if tenant queue exceeds high watermark

Example policy table
| Metric trigger | Action | Timeout | Owner |
| Q_DEPTH > 200 | Truncate context (preserve last 512 tokens) | 30s | inference-runtime-team |
| p95 > 400ms | Switch to variant v-fast-8q | 60s | model-onboarding-team |
| token-rate > plan_cap | Return 429 + Retry-After | 5s | billing-integrations |

Configuration schema (YAML) - sample
```yaml
shaping:
  hard_limits:
    max_payload_tokens: 120000
    max_seq_len: 512000
  thresholds:
    queue_depth_high: 200
    p95_latency_ms: 400
  actions:
    - name: truncate_context
      preserve_tail_tokens: 512
      duration_seconds: 30
    - name: switch_variant
      target_variant: "v-fast-8q"
      duration_seconds: 60
    - name: throttle
      retry_after_seconds: 5
```

Observability and feedback loop
- Calculate 5m rolling windows for the SLOs and shaping KPIs.
- The feedback controller uses two inputs: latency residual and cost residual.
  - latency residual = max(0, observed_p99 - target_p99) mapped to [0,1].
  - cost residual = (observed_tokens_per_gpu - target_tokens_per_gpu) / target_tokens_per_gpu.
- Controller adjusts per-tenant token-rate caps and variant-affinity weights every 30s using a PID-style controller with conservative gains.

Suggested monitoring queries (PromQL examples)
- p95 latency (route=my-route): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- token rate per GPU: sum(rate(request_payload_tokens[1m])) by (gpu_id)
- shaping action rate: sum(rate(shaping_action_count[1m])) by (action)

Alerting and runbook thresholds
- P1: p99 > 1.2 * target_p99 for 10m AND shaping.action != 0 -> page SRE and inference-runtime oncall.
- P2: error rate > 2% for 5m -> notify product-owner and oncall.
- P3: sustained cost residual > 0.6 for 1h -> cost ops + finance alert (email).

Incident playbook (summary)
1) Triage: confirm scope (tenant vs global). Check model.variant_in_use tag and queue_depth by tenant.
2) Mitigate: apply emergency shaping profile (reject non-critical routes, switch to smallest quantized variant, enable prefix caching).
3) Stabilize: once p95 < target for 15m, progressively lift emergency measures in reverse order.
4) Postmortem: attach shaping.config used during incident, delta in token cost, timeline of actions.

Safety and API contract guidance
- When switching variants, ensure structured-response contract (response.schema_version) remains compatible. Use response.metadata.variant_replacement to record change.
- Errors should include machine-readable 'redwood_error' field with keys: code, retryable, suggestion. Example: {"code":"THROTTLED_TOKENS","retryable":true,"suggestion":"reduce prompt size or retry after 5s"}

Rollout and review cadence
- All shaping strategies require: unit test suite, canary (1% traffic for 24h), metrics review, and a staged rollout to 25%/50%/100%.
- Policy ownership: inference-runtime-team. Review cadence: quarterly or after any incident triggering P1.

Owner and contacts
- Primary owner: inference-runtime-team (oncall: #inference-runtime-oncall)
- Secondary: model-onboarding-team
- Cost ops: finance-ops@redwood.example.com

Appendix: example diagnostics snippet (CLI)
```bash
# Query tenant queue depth and top routes
redwood-admin metrics query "sum by (tenant, route) (rate(tenant_queue_depth[1m]))" --tenant=acme
# Apply emergency shaping profile for tenant
redwood-admin shaping apply --tenant acme --profile emergency-truncate-512
```
